name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
attention_variant: MLA variant with compressed/hashed KV (sliding_window 128, compress_ratios), sparse indexer index_topk 512; kv_lora_rank absent from config
notes: The biggest serving-economics jump in this slice, and the one field I could NOT fully derive. Vendor: 284B total / 13B activated, 1M context (max_position_embeddings 1048576 via YaRN factor 16 over an original 65536 - a much smaller extension factor than V3's 40). kv_cache_bytes_per_token is null because kv_lora_rank is ABSENT from the V4 config. V4 replaces the plain MLA latent with a compressed/quantized cache: config has expert_dtype fp4, hc_mult 4, num_hash_layers 3, o_lora_rank 1024, a per-layer compress_ratios array that is mostly 4 (interleaved with 128 every 5th layer), compress_rope_theta 160000, and sliding_window 128. A reader should NOT assume the V3 latent formula carries over; the geometry is genuinely different and needs the V4 modeling code to state precisely. Architecture is otherwise DeepSeek-V3-like: 43 layers (not 61), hidden 4096, 256 routed + 1 shared expert, 6 per token (not 8), moe_intermediate_size 2048, q_lora_rank 1024, head_dim 512 with qk_rope_head_dim 64, num_key_value_heads 1. Weights ship pre-quantized (fp8 e4m3, 128x128 block) so the bf16 total is smaller than a naive 284B suggests. MIT.
